posts.author: bass2yang
posts.body:
Try this inside the damage formula:
JavaScript:
let dmg = a.hp - 1; a.gainHp(-dmg); dmg
That way, it will show the user's HP sacrificed to damage the target. If it is a miss, no damage will be evaluated.
Edit: if you are doing an action sequence of some sort before the attack (like a Vegeta style explosion against Majin Boo), you may want to store the "hp-1" inside a control variable and then call it inside the damage formula and proceed from there (like v[15] for variable 15).

If you are typing in the % sign, that is the modulo operator used to give you the remainder and giving you an error (it is expecting a number after the % sign to complete the equation - you won't need it here since it will not do what you are intending to do). In the case of the damage formula, any error forces it to return 0 as a safety net.
Also, based on what you are doing, the user is losing the same amount as the damage. However, based on what you are describing, you only want to sacrifice 10% of your HP to deal 5 times attack + 2 times the 10% of HP used.
Try this:
JavaScript:
let dmg = a.atk*5 + 2*(a.hp*.1); a.gainHp(-a.hp*.1); dmg

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Just to interject into the help that
@bass2yang
is giving - it's important to provide a disclaimer about putting things like this into the damage formula.
If you:
- have battlers on Auto Battle with these skills, or
- give these skills to enemies
it can cause the the HP draining to happen multiple times a turn, or even if the skill isn't used.
The damage formula is executed internally as a part of the process to determine which skill is best by the engine's AI, so putting functions like that that do something besides contribute to the damage calculation will just happen.
That's why it's better practice to put them into notetags as I showed in the thread linked to in the first post. The skill would work fine using that code if the equivalent VisuStella notetags were used.
Tennshii said:
Would it also be possible for the hp loss to round to the nearest whole number?
Click to expand...
You'd change that portion of the formula to
a.gainHp(Math.round(-a.hp*.1))
You may want to do that both places so the multiplier is the same as what's lost.

posts.author: Kenen
posts.body:
Tennshii said:
I'm not entirely sure what this means.
Click to expand...
The game will evaluate damage formulas under certain scenarios, e.g. when hashing out enemy AI.
Anything within those damage formulas that directly alters a battler's attributes via a method, e.g. "a.gainHp(-a.hp*.1)" gets executed during those evaluations, even if the skill doesn't actually get used in battle.
It's okay to use those types of methods in your damage formulas, but you want to be careful to ensure that the related skills aren't being evaluated by the engine, either via enemy AI, actor auto-battle, or the eval() method in a plugin.
